name: Cash-Economy Skimming and Sales Suppression
description: Cash-intensive businesses underreport takings through suppressed sales records, electronic sales suppression tools or diverting cash from the till. The unreported cash is spent outside the banking system, deposited in structured amounts or moved offshore.

sources.text: OECD, Electronic Sales Suppression: A Threat to Tax Revenues (2013)
OECD, Shining Light on the Shadow Economy: Opportunities and Threats (2017)
FATF/OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)
FATF and OECD, Money Laundering Awareness Handbook for Tax Examiners and Tax Auditors (2012)

indicators.name: Declared turnover lower than card and bank takings imply
indicators.canon: Declared turnover lower than card and bank takings imply
indicators.desc: Card acquiring volumes or supplier purchases suggest higher sales than the business reports to authorities.
indicators.ctx: Card acquiring volumes or supplier purchases suggest higher sales than the business reports to authorities.
indicators.fp: Timing differences, refunds and tips affect reconciliation.

indicators.name: Cash deposits well below expected for business type
indicators.canon: Cash deposits well below expected for business type
indicators.desc: A business with high card use but little cash banking, despite sector norms of cash trade.
indicators.ctx: A business with high card use but little cash banking, despite sector norms of cash trade.
indicators.fp: Cash may be used to pay suppliers legitimately.

indicators.name: Cash used to pay suppliers and wages directly
indicators.canon: Cash used to pay suppliers and wages directly
indicators.desc: Owner pays suppliers, rent or staff in cash taken from takings before banking.
indicators.ctx: Owner pays suppliers, rent or staff in cash taken from takings before banking.
indicators.fp: Small suppliers sometimes insist on cash.

indicators.name: Structured cash deposits across branches or accounts
indicators.canon: Cash deposits split across branches, ATMs or accounts
indicators.desc: Cash is deposited in several locations, channels or accounts on the same day or over a short period so that no single deposit stands out.
indicators.ctx: Cash banked in many amounts just below reporting thresholds, often across multiple branches or personal accounts.
indicators.fp: Some businesses make routine daily deposits in small sums.

indicators.name: POS software with sales-suppression features or tampered records
indicators.canon: POS software with sales-suppression features or tampered records
indicators.desc: Use of unfamiliar till software, offline mode usage, or missing sequential receipts.
indicators.ctx: Use of unfamiliar till software, offline mode usage, or missing sequential receipts.
indicators.fp: Software glitches or offline trading can cause gaps.

indicators.name: High refund or void rates on card terminals
indicators.canon: High refund or void rates on card terminals
indicators.desc: Frequent voids and cash refunds conceal sales.
indicators.ctx: Frequent voids and cash refunds conceal sales.

indicators.name: Owner lifestyle inconsistent with declared profits
indicators.canon: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means
indicators.desc: Assets, lifestyle spending or purchases clearly exceed the customer's known legitimate income or declared wealth, with no verifiable source.
indicators.ctx: Spending, assets and property purchases exceed what reported profits could support.
indicators.fp: Family wealth or gifts could explain this.

indicators.name: Cash transferred to offshore through MVTS or cash couriers
indicators.canon: Cash transferred to offshore through MVTS or cash couriers
indicators.desc: Cash takings leave the country via money transfer, hawala-style networks or couriers.
indicators.ctx: Cash takings leave the country via money transfer, hawala-style networks or couriers.
indicators.fp: Diaspora remittance is common and lawful.
